accuracy.evidence: The process follows the CASEL definition of responsible decision-making (identifying problems, generating solutions, anticipating and evaluating consequences for self and others, reflecting) and the topic's IB PYP PSPE outcome (stop to think, identify options, consider consequences, then choose). The adult text's claim that inhibitory control is a core executive function still developing through childhood is from Diamond (2013, Annual Review of Psychology). Stop Think Do is named as an example routine (Petersen and Adderley), described only in outline. Scenario consequences are plausible and age-appropriate, and none presents one option as the only possible outcome: the cards say 'may own up' and 'most likely'. The sweets arithmetic (10 sweets, eat 2, save 8; p4 n minus 2) was checked at the range corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the impulsive-choice errors listed in CASEL guidance and social problem-solving research (Spivack and Shure's interpersonal cognitive problem solving: generating alternatives and anticipating consequences): acting on the first idea (STOP step, p1, m1, challenge 'first'), only one option (step 1 prediction, m2, challenge 'one'), only now and not later (sweets timeline, m3, m8, challenge 'now'), only me (m4, m7, challenge 'me'), reasons that are not about consequences (step 4, p5, challenge 'reason') and giving up when a choice fails (step 5, m6, challenge 'quit').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstc is about the decision process itself: a first idea that slides toward DO IT unless the child taps a STOP sign, an options list that grows from one to four, an option-to-consequence matching board, a now-tomorrow-next-week slider that changes two outcome bars, a choose-then-justify board, and a what-next board after a choice fails. flagcool is about how strong feelings narrow choices and cooling off, flagdecide teaches the vocabulary of consequences and safety for ages 5 to 8, and flagdilem weighs two values in an ethical dilemma; none times a first idea, matches options to consequences or compares short- and long-term results on a timeline. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step makes the child do the part of the process before the text names it: if they do not stop, the first idea reaches DO IT and the brother cries; after stopping, three more options appear; wrong consequence matches explain what that option really leads to; the bars flip as the dot moves from now to next week; a first-idea or someone-asked reason is refused with why; and grabbing or sulking after a no is refused in favour of a new option.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab disproves: 'Just one: my first idea' (four options appear), 'Yes, always' for the choice that feels best now (the eat-all bar drops to not good tomorrow and next week), and 'Give up: thinking did not help' (two good next tries are found).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; each wrong option carries one of six distinct messages naming the slip: acting on a first idea, only one option, only now, a reason that is not about what will happen, giving up or repeating after a failure, and thinking only of yourself. Answer order rotates between questions.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs walk through the steps in short sentences with plain words (stop, options, what might happen, choose and know why); the adult text was rewritten into shorter sentences to pass the 9.5 grade limit and names CASEL responsible decision-making, the IB PYP PSPE outcome, inhibitory control and the key vocabulary. Card texts are short. validate_lessons readability passes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one step: stop, options, consequences now and later and for others, choose with a reason and retry. Items cover stopping (p1, m1), options (p2, m2, m5), consequences (p3, m3, m4, m8), reasons (p5), saving for later (p4), fair options for a group (m7), a cheating secret (m9) and retrying (m6).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 light, 360 px Android light and dark and desktop dark screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me. The STOP sign is at least 70 px across with a hit radius larger than the sign; the DO IT box and the sliding first idea fit on one lane at 360 px; the matching columns keep four cards each with readable wrapped text; the time slider knob is 26 px across and snaps to three stops; option and reason cards stack in one column on phones. Real taps on STOP, the matching drag and the slider drag were tested.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: STOP, add each option, pick an option then a consequence (each consequence button is labelled with the option it is for), Later and Sooner for the timeline plus one Choose button per choice, choose then reason buttons, and one button per next try. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with what happened and why. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
